parts.title: My home is an island
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
I live on a tiny island in the north of Scotland. Only two hundred people live here, and most of us know each other well. Our school has just twelve pupils, and I am in the same class as my little cousin.

The ferry is the most important thing in our lives. It comes three times a week, and it brings food, post and visitors. If the weather is bad, it cannot sail, and then we have to wait. Last winter, there was no ferry for nine days, and the shop ran out of bread!

Some people think that island life must be boring, but I disagree. After school, I go to the beach with my friends to look for crabs and shells. In the evening, we play football on the grass by the church. In summer, the sun does not go down until almost midnight.

Of course, there are some things I miss. There is no cinema, and the nearest big town is three hours away by boat and bus. When I am eighteen, I will probably go to university on the mainland. But I know that I will always come back, because this is my home.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about her school?
options: It is closed during the winter months
It has only twelve pupils in total
It is in the same building as the church
It has two hundred pupils in total
questions.explanation: Our school has just twelve pupils.

questions.prompt: What happened last winter?
options: The ferry could not sail for nine days
The shop was closed for a week
A big storm broke the pier
The island lost its power for a day
questions.explanation: There was no ferry for nine days, and the shop ran out of bread.

questions.prompt: What does she do after school?
options: She helps her cousin with homework
She works in the island shop
She looks for crabs and shells
questions.explanation: She goes to the beach with friends to look for crabs and shells.

questions.prompt: What does she miss about the mainland?
options: A football pitch near the church
questions.explanation: There is no cinema on the island.

questions.prompt: What does the writer think about her future?
options: She will leave and never return
She will return to her home one day
She will start a business on the island
She will become a ferry captain
questions.explanation: She says she will always come back, because this is her home.

parts.title: A holiday on a tiny island
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Coral Cay is a tiny island in the Caribbean. It is only two kilometres long, and you can walk all the way round it in about an hour. [1] There are no big hotels, no cars and no traffic lights.

Most visitors arrive on the little boat from the larger island. [2] The journey takes thirty minutes, and passengers often see dolphins on the way.

There are only five places to sleep on the island. [3] Most of them have a view of the sea from every window, and the owners cook breakfast for each guest.

During the day, visitors swim, rest in the shade or take a small boat to a nearby reef. [4] The water is so clear that you can see the fish from the beach.

In the evening, everyone eats together on the sand. [5] Many people say that it is the most relaxing holiday they have ever had.
sentences: Even in the hottest weather, there is a nice cool breeze.
All of them are small family houses near the beach.
Visitors can rent a bicycle on the larger island.
Afterwards, they sit and watch the stars come out.
This makes it one of the quietest places that you can find.
The ferry from the mainland takes three hours.
It leaves every morning at nine and returns at five.
There are many shops in the centre of the capital.

gaps.explanation: The island is tiny, so it is one of the quietest places, and the next sentence lists what it does not have.
The boat leaving at nine matches "the little boat", and the journey then takes thirty minutes.
The five places to sleep are small family houses, which explains the owners and the sea views.
The breeze after swimming and resting in the shade connects to the clear water in the next sentence.
Watching the stars after eating together leads to the comment on a relaxing holiday.

parts.title: Why people love islands
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Islands have always been popular places for holidays. People like them [1] they are often quiet and beautiful. On a small island, you can leave your bike outside your door, and nobody will take it. Life moves [2] a slower speed, and people have time to talk to each other. [3] you are tired of busy cities, an island holiday can be a perfect rest. However, living on an island is not always easy. Everything has to come [4] boat, so shopping can be expensive. Young people sometimes leave to find work on the mainland, and [5] is a problem for small communities. Even so, those [6] stay usually say that they would not live anywhere else.

gaps.explanation: People like them because they are quiet: reason.
If you are tired of busy cities: condition.
The preposition "by" goes with transport: come by boat.
This is a problem refers back to young people leaving.
Those who stay: relative pronoun for people.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Good morning, passengers. A short reminder about the ferry timetable for the island. During the week, the first ferry leaves at eight, and that is the one that most workers take. On Sundays, it is different. The ferry does not go at eight, because the crew has a day off, and the service is slower. It leaves at nine, and not at ten, as some people think, because ten is the time for the boat to the next island. I know that the timetable at the harbour office still shows the old time, so please ignore it and be at the quay early.

question.prompt: When does the ferry leave on Sundays?
question.explanation: Eight is the weekday ferry and ten is the boat to another island; on Sundays the ferry leaves at nine.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Alfonso, have you tried the café at the harbour? Everybody says that it’s the place to go.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I went on Friday. The chairs were hard, and you sit outside in the wind, so that wasn’t comfortable. And it isn’t cheap, either, it cost me more than my hotel breakfast.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Then why is it so popular?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Because of the soup. They make it every morning from the fish that the boats bring in, with potatoes and a bit of cream. It’s thick, and it tastes of the sea. I had two bowls.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Now I’m hungry. Shall we go?

question.prompt: What is special about the harbour café?
options: Its prices are quite low indeed
Its chairs are very soft and big
question.explanation: He says the chairs are hard and the café is not cheap, but the soup made from the morning catch is what makes it special.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Hello, Aleksander, it’s Alessia. I’m on the boat, and I had to tell you about the dolphins. The captain said that the week before he saw five, jumping all around the boat, so I was hoping for a big group. In the first hour I only saw two, far away near the rocks, and I took a blurry photo. I was disappointed, but then, near the end of the trip, a group came right up to the side. I counted them carefully, and there were three. It was a magical moment. I’ll show you the video later.

question.prompt: How many dolphins did the woman see?
question.explanation: The captain saw five last week, she saw two at the start, but a group came near the end and she counted three.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: The water looks lovely, Amaru. Is it warm enough for a swim now? It’s only eight o’clock.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Not yet. In the morning it’s cold, because the night cooled it down. You’d shiver for ten minutes.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: What about the evening? We could go after dinner.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: By then the sun has gone and the wind comes up, so it feels fresh again. The warmest time is the afternoon, when the sun has been on it for hours. I always swim at about three.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Great, I’ll wait until then and read my book.

question.explanation: The morning water is cold from the night, and the evening is cool after sunset; the afternoon is the warmest because of the sun.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Welcome to Blue Wave Ferries. Before you go to the gate, please listen carefully. Many of you have asked if you need your bank card to show at the gate, but we only use it at the café, where you pay for coffee. Some travellers think they must bring a passport, but that is only for trips abroad, and this ferry stays inside the country. What every passenger needs is the printed paper that we sent by email yesterday evening. Without it, the staff cannot let you on the boat. Have a pleasant journey.

question.prompt: What must passengers show at the gate?
question.explanation: The bank card is used at the café and the passport is for trips abroad; every passenger must show the paper they printed from the email, which is the ticket.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Hi, Alexei, it’s Allegra. Don’t be surprised when you see my bag. I made a lot of sandwiches this morning. You know that I get hungry quite quickly, and my brother always laughs at me, but that is not why I’m doing this. The sandwiches in the market yesterday were cheap, and I thought about buying some, but then I remembered that there is nothing to eat where we are going. No shop, no café, just rocks and birds on the island. So bring something too, and plenty of water.

question.prompt: Why has the man brought sandwiches?
options: They were cheap in the market
question.explanation: She admits that she gets hungry and that the sandwiches in the market were cheap, but the reason is that there is no shop on the island.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Can’t you stay one more day, Alisha? The weather’s going to be perfect on Sunday.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I’d love to. I called the hotel, and they said they have rooms for the weekend, so that isn’t a problem. And the ferry runs as normal, even with the wind.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: So what’s the matter?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I’m back at the office on Monday morning at eight. I have a big meeting with a customer, and I haven’t finished the report. I can’t miss it.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: What a pity. Come back in the summer, then.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I will. I promise.

question.prompt: Why can't the woman stay longer?
question.explanation: The hotel has rooms and the ferry is running; she must be at work on Monday morning for a meeting.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: How was your first sailing lesson, Aleksander? I thought you’d be terrified.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I was a little, before we left the harbour. But the waves weren’t big and the instructor stayed next to me.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Ouch! My back is red and it really hurts. I forgot the cream.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: You look like a lobster. It’s not that serious, though. You don’t need a doctor, I had the same thing last year and a cold shower helped.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Should I buy a hat? I’ve lost mine.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: A hat is good for your head, but your back is the problem. Just stay inside or under the umbrella tomorrow, and wear a loose shirt. Give your skin a day to rest.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I suppose you’re right. It’s a boring plan but it’s sensible.

options: Stay out of the sun tomorrow
question.explanation: She says a doctor is not necessary and a hat would not protect his back; the plan is to keep out of the sun for a day.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: So, Ainsley, how is your room? I thought you’d be disappointed because it’s so small.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: It is small, but I don’t mind that. I only sleep there. And the view of the sea is beautiful, that’s a good point.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Is something wrong, then?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Yes, the bar underneath. There’s loud music every night until two in the morning, and last night I didn’t sleep at all. I’m going to ask for another room.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Poor you. Tell the manager today.

question.prompt: How does Ainsley feel about the hotel room?
question.explanation: He does not mind the size and likes the view, but he complains about the loud music from the bar every night.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: There’s a storm coming, Alexei, so we can’t dive tomorrow. I’m sorry, I know you were looking forward to it.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Don’t worry about it. I’m not angry. Honestly, I’m quite relieved.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Really? I thought you’d be upset about losing a day.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: We’ve been up at six every morning this week, and my legs are tired. A day with a book and a hot chocolate sounds perfect. And the boat is in the harbour, so it’s safe.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: You’re very calm about it.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I’ve learned to be.

question.prompt: How does Alexei feel about the storm?
question.explanation: Alisha thinks he will be upset, but he is tired after early mornings and is happy for a day of rest.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I saw you at the fish stall at six this morning, Allegra. Do you really start that early?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Every day. I carry the boxes from the boats, put ice on the fish, and talk to customers. It’s heavy, and I’m wet and cold all day.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I couldn’t do it. It’s not boring, there’s always something happening, and I’m sure the money’s fine, but I’d be exhausted.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: You get used to it. I love it, honestly.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I admire you. I’d never get up so early.

question.prompt: What does Alfonso think about Allegra's job?
question.explanation: He says it is not boring and the money is probably good, but he thinks he would be exhausted, so he sees it as hard work.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: What shall we do on Saturday, Alessia? I could teach a swimming class for the children.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: That’s kind, but the pool is closed that weekend. And I wanted to go to town by boat, but the shops will be shut because of the holiday.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I got a message from the council. They need volunteers to clean the beach after the storm.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: That’s a better idea. It’s good exercise and the beach is dirty. Let’s bring gloves and bags.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’ll text the others.

question.prompt: What do Aleksander and Alessia agree to do on Saturday?
question.explanation: The pool is closed and the shops are shut, so they agree to help clean the beach after the storm.

parts.title: A talk about Iceland
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: sigrun
turns.text: Good morning, everyone. In today’s lesson, I will tell you about Iceland, a large island in the North Atlantic Ocean. It is a small country in terms of people. Some students think that millions of people live there, but only about four hundred thousand live in the whole country. About a third of them live in the capital, which has a population of a hundred and thirty thousand. The capital city is called Reykjavik. It is not the oldest town, but it is the largest. Another city, Akureyri, is in the north, but it is much smaller. Iceland is also famous for its nature. It has glaciers and lakes, but what visitors remember are the volcanoes. There are more than a hundred of them, and some are still active. Under the ground, the earth is very hot, and Icelanders use this heat for their houses and for swimming. Their hot pools are heated by the ground, so people sit in warm water outside, even in snow. This is cheap and clean. Now let me talk about food. Icelanders love lamb, which is cooked in many ways. But the most popular food is fish, which people have eaten for hundreds of years, because the sea is so rich. A traditional dish is fish soup, and in the supermarkets you can see many kinds of fish. And the last topic, the sky. In summer, the sun hardly sets, so you can read at midnight. But in winter, the nights are long, and on clear nights, you may see the northern lights, with green and pink colours moving across the sky. It is something that nobody forgets. I recommend visiting from September to March for the best chance. Thank you for listening.

gaps.prompt: The number of people in the country is about ___
gaps.explanation: Only about four hundred thousand live in the country; the capital has a hundred and thirty thousand.

gaps.prompt: The largest city, where about a third of the people live, is ___
gaps.explanation: The capital is Reykjavik; Akureyri in the north is much smaller.

gaps.prompt: Visitors remember the more than a hundred ___
gaps.explanation: There are glaciers and lakes, but visitors remember the volcanoes, more than a hundred of them.

gaps.prompt: People enjoy warm outdoor pools because the ___ heats them
gaps.explanation: The pools are heated by the ground; the heat comes from under the earth.

gaps.prompt: The food that Icelanders eat most is ___
gaps.explanation: They love lamb, but the most popular food is fish.

gaps.prompt: On clear winter nights it is possible to see the northern ___
gaps.explanation: In winter you may see the northern lights with green and pink colours.

parts.title: An interview with a lighthouse keeper
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Ainsley, you live alone on a small island. How did you get there in the first place?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: Not through my work, my company never sent me there. And I didn’t buy a house after a holiday, I couldn’t afford one. I came as a volunteer for one summer to help repair the tower, and I never left. That was eight years ago, and I still enjoy it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you do every week?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: There are a lot of jobs. The tower needs painting, but we do that once a year, in the spring. And the boats belong to the fishermen, I don’t repair them. Every week I clean the light. Salt covers the glass and the light cannot shine well, so I wash it by hand. It takes a whole morning.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you ever feel lonely?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: Sometimes, in the dark months. I don’t plan to move to the city, I’d hate it. And I only go to town for supplies once a month. The thing that helps is the neighbours, and honestly, I talk to the radio a lot too, which is a bit silly. Three families live on the island, and every Sunday we have lunch together at somebody’s house, so I know I’ll see them.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you like best about island life?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: I know people say the food from the garden is special, and the beach is a short walk from my door, which is lovely. But what I like best is the quiet. There are no cars, no phones ringing, only the sound of the sea. It clears my head.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What happened last winter?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: We had a terrible storm in January. The boat that brings food came as usual, so that wasn’t the problem, and the light kept working all night. But the wind broke one of my windows. I stuck a board over it and sat in the kitchen with three jumpers on. It was scary, and I admit that I was thinking about the old keepers who lived through worse winters than this one.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do tourists visit the lighthouse?

turns.speaker: k
turns.text: In summer, yes, and I love it. I take them to the top of the tower, and the view is incredible. I don’t serve them tea, I’m too busy, and I’m not good at telling long stories. I let the view speak, and most of them go quiet at the top, which I love to see. Some of them even cry, and that always surprises me.

questions.prompt: Why did Ainsley first come to the island?
questions.explanation: His company did not send him and he could not afford a house; he came as a volunteer to help repair the tower.

questions.prompt: What does he do every week?
questions.explanation: Painting is done once a year and he does not repair the boats; every week he washes the salt off the light.

questions.prompt: What does he do so that he does not feel lonely?

He plans to move to the city

questions.explanation: He does not plan to move or go to town often; the Sunday lunches with neighbours help.

questions.prompt: What does he like best about island life?
questions.explanation: He says that the garden food and the beach are nice, but the quiet and the sound of the sea are the best.

questions.prompt: What happened last year in the winter?

questions.explanation: The boat came as usual and the light kept working; the wind broke a window.

questions.explanation: He takes tourists to the top of the tower; he does not serve tea or tell long stories.
